C-WINDOWS-MENU-ACCELERATORS.Name: Windows/Linux menu-accelerator rescue — implementation plan
C-WINDOWS-MENU-ACCELERATORS.IntentSummary: Add src/renderer/src/services/windowMenuAccelerators.js: a non-macOS window-level capture keydown dispatcher holding the audited table of 22 menu chords (Ctrl+S/N/O/W/P/F/H/G/D/B/M, Shift-variants, Alt+Ctrl+V, the mode trio, tab cycles) mapped to existing command registry ids, with IMe/repeat guards, physical event.code matching, and input-surface carve-outs; wire it once at boot in app.vue beside the existing zoom/palette capture handlers; reuse menu-bridge's findCommandById for dispatch. Unit tests pin table-registry parity and an m009_menu.rs source cross-check (win-relevant accelerators vs table, alive-excluded absent); a chromium e2e spec with the platform stubbed win32 proves chord dispatch end-to-end (source mode + chip, save, close tab) and darwin silence; the Windows acceptance protocol doc carries the FIX-2 errata and corrected probe recipe; graph M-070 / verification V-M-070 land with the module; the polygon round (NSIS rebuild + real cua hotkeys) closes the acceptance effect.

T-001.Title: windowMenuAccelerators module: chord table, matcher, dispatcher, guards

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: WINDOW_MENU_ACCELERATORS lists exactly the 22 audited chords (spec Goal-2 list) as { accelerator, commandId } entries; the table is a frozen const and every commandId resolves through the static command registry imported from commands/index.js — no ids that the registry or its subcommands do not define.

matchAccelerator(event) maps a KeyboardEvent to a normalized accelerator string using physical event.code (KeyS→S, Digit0→0, Backslash, Tab, Equal, Minus) with Ctrl/Alt/Shift modifier sets, layout-independent, reusing the house getAcceleratorFromKeyboardEvent normalization where it fits; a modifier-only or composing (isComposing) or auto-repeat event never matches.

The dispatcher runs as a window capture keydown listener: on a match it preventDefaults, resolves the command via menu-bridge's now-exported findCommandById and executes it (execute() or executeSubcommand fallback, identical to the mt::menu-invoked bridge path), skipping when the event target sits inside a non-editor input surface for the chords where the browser default is correct (at minimum Ctrl+A inside input/textarea outside the editor surface); unmatched events pass through untouched.

installWindowMenuAccelerators() is a no-op returning a noop disposer when isOsx is true (mac's native menu owns the chords); on win/linux it registers the listener and returns its disposer. MODULE_CONTRACT (PURPOSE/SCOPE/DEPENDS/LINKS M-070), MODULE_MAP and CHANGE_SUMMARY v1.0.0 C-WINDOWS-MENU-ACCELERATORS blocks are present.

T-002.Title: app.vue boot wiring beside the existing capture handlers

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: installWindowMenuAccelerators() is called once during app setup directly beside setupZoomKeysFontSize/setupCommandPaletteShortcut with its disposer handled the same way, and app.vue's CHANGE_SUMMARY advances with C-WINDOWS-MENU-ACCELERATORS.

No other component or store is touched: sidebar Ctrl+\, zoom trio and palette binding keep their existing owners; the new listener adds no duplicate handling for them (they are absent from the table).

T-003.Title: Unit tests: registry parity, guards, gates, m009 source cross-check

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Every table entry's commandId exists in the static registry (depth-first incl. subcommands); the excluded chords are asserted absent (Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0, Cmd+, / Cmd+Q / Cmd+Shift+P, Ctrl+CmdOrCtrl+F).

The m009 cross-check reads src-tauri/src/m009_menu.rs, extracts every win-relevant declared accelerator (CmdOrCtrl/Ctrl/Alt forms), normalizes them the same way the matcher does, and asserts the table equals that set minus the documented exclusions — drift in either direction fails CI.

Guard tests: isOsx gate (no listener on darwin), IME composing, auto-repeat, Ctrl+A carve-out inside a sidebar input, and a dispatch test proving the matched chord executes the registry command exactly once with preventDefault called.

T-004.Title: E2E: chord dispatch on a win32-stubbed platform, silence on darwin

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: tests/e2e/windows-accelerators.spec.ts runs on the chromium tauri-shim project with the platform stubbed win32: Ctrl+Alt+S turns sourceCode on and the titlebar mode chip renders; Ctrl+S saves a dirty document (content reaches disk or the save command marker fires per the house e2e save pattern); Ctrl+W closes the focused tab.
The same spec proves the darwin-stubbed run leaves the chords unhandled by the new dispatcher (commands not executed through it), pinning the macOS no-op gate.

T-005.Title: Acceptance protocol errata: FIX-2 reclassification and corrected probe recipe

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: docs/acceptance/cua-e2e-windows-polygon.md gains the FIX-2 errata (measurement phantom: silent ipcRenderer.invoke no-op dispatcher + loose resting-state selectors; chips proven functional by pinia probe) and replaces the round recipe with: strict chip selector .titlebar-mode-chips-wrap .mode-chip, pinia-state assertions for mode engagement, dispatch via the mt::menu-invoked Tauri event emit, real-input accelerator testing via cua hotkey with delivery_mode foreground, and the 125% desktop-scale coordinate trap note.

T-006.Title: Graph and verification entries: M-070 / V-M-070

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: .grace/graph/runtime.xml gains M-070 for the module with its contract-linked summary; .grace/verification/runtime.xml gains V-M-070 with scenarios covering table parity, dispatch, gates and the polygon hotkey round; both route consistently with the existing m009/menu-bridge/app.vue links.

T-007.Title: Polygon acceptance: NSIS rebuild + real-input hotkey round

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Branch build on the polygon (house NSIS recipe, createUpdaterArtifacts off) + silent reinstall; real cua hotkey Ctrl+Alt+S (delivery_mode foreground) turns Source Code Mode on with the mode chip rendered in the titlebar; Ctrl+S writes a dirty scratch document (mtime moves); Ctrl+N opens a tab; Ctrl+Tab cycles when more than one tab is open — if WebView2 swallows the chord, the two tab-cycle entries are dropped to a documented follow-up and the rest stands.
Round evidence lands in the acceptance folder (probe outputs + screenshots) and the ☰ click path is re-verified from real rect coordinates (menu opens).
